newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil literacy crusader Paulo Freire dies.
newsitem.headline: Brazil literacy crusader Paulo Freire dies.

text.p: Brazilian educator Paulo Freire, who gained international acclaim for an innovative method of teaching adults how to read and write, died on Friday at the age of 75, a hospital spokesman said.
Freire, the author of 25 books on literacy, was admitted to Albert Einstein hospital in Sao Paulo on Thursday for heart problems, the spokesman said. He did not give a precise cause of death.
Among Freire's works, which were translated in up to 30 languages, are "Education as a Practice of Freedom" and "Pedagogy of the Oppressed.
Born in a country with one of the highest illiteracy rates in the world, Freire developed a method for teaching mainly poor adults how to read and write.
His technique, which was first used in 1961 in his home state of Pernambuco in northeastern Brazil, was based on the critical analysis of social, economic and political problems in Brazil.
Freire founded the Institute for Cultural Action in France and received honorary degrees from universities in Europe and the United States.
